## 3. What the signals said
The SMA-20/SMA-50 crossover system fired 1 golden crosses (2026-04-27) and 2 death crosses (2026-01-20, 2026-08-14). Crossovers are lagging by construction — they confirm a trend that has already started, so they miss the first few percent of every move. That lag is exactly why the backtest below matters: it prices in the cost of being late.

## 4. Strategy backtest verdict
A naive 'hold when SMA_20 > SMA_50, else cash' rule returned -14.2% versus -10.2% for simply buying and holding — it trailed buy-and-hold by 4.0 points. Risk-adjusted, the strategy's Sharpe ratio was -0.67 with a worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -22.9%. Take this as a teaching result, not a trading system: it ignores brokerage, taxes, slippage, and the fact that it sat in cash during rallies it failed to catch. Real edges are rarely this clean.

## 5. ML direction model — honest assessment
The next-day direction classifier (LogisticRegression on 7 lagged technical features) scored 53.5% accuracy on the last 43 trading days, which did not beat the always-guess-the-majority-class baseline of 62.8%. Most influential features by |coefficient|: bb_pos (0.5289), vol_change (0.2647), ret_1 (0.2339). Honest read: predicting next-day direction from past prices is barely better than a coin flip even on clean synthetic data — on real markets, transaction costs would eat the rest. The model's real value here is pedagogical: it shows the full ML workflow (feature engineering, chronological split to avoid look-ahead bias, honest baseline) on time-series data.

## 6. Risks & caveats (read before acting on any of this)
- **Synthetic data.** Regimes, the shock, and the rally were scripted; real markets
  are adversarial and regime shifts are not announced in advance.
- **No costs modelled.** Brokerage, STT, slippage, and taxes are all zero here and
  very much non-zero in reality.
- **Lagging indicators.** SMAs, RSI, and MACD all describe the past. They manage
  risk; they do not predict the future.
- **Overfitting danger.** Parameters (20/50/14/2σ) were chosen by convention, not
  optimized — which is actually a virtue here: tuning them on this one dataset
  would just memorize noise.
